subject.number-theory.title: Number theory
subject.number-theory.define: Arithmetic from divisibility to number fields, local fields, prime distribution and rational points.
subject.number-theory.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.number-theory.assumed_background: Abstract algebra including rings and fields, elementary group theory, complex analysis for analytic topics.
subject.number-theory.learning_outcomes:
- Distinguish element factorization, prime-ideal factorization and class groups.
- Connect global arithmetic with completions and ramification.
- Separate proven distribution theorems from stronger error estimates and conjectures.
subject.number-theory.study_route: [Euclidean algorithm and unique factorization](./notes/nt.divisibility.md) → [Chinese remainder theorem](./notes/nt.crt.md) → [Finite fields](./notes/nt.finite-fields.md) → [Number fields, norm and trace](./notes/nt.number-fields.md) → [Algebraic integers](./notes/nt.integers.md) → [Dedekind domains and ideal factorization](./notes/nt.ideals.md) → [Ideal class group](./notes/nt.class-group.md) → [p-adic numbers and Hensel lifting](./notes/nt.padic.md) → [Riemann zeta function](./notes/nt.zeta.md)

nt.divisibility.title: Euclidean algorithm and unique factorization
nt.divisibility.define: The Euclidean algorithm underlies Bezout identities and unique integer factorization.
nt.divisibility.statement: Every integer greater than one factors uniquely into primes up to order. For integers a,b not both zero, their positive gcd is $ua+vb$ for some integers u,v.
nt.divisibility.hypotheses: Factorization is in the ordinary integers.
nt.divisibility.caution: Unique factorization of elements may fail in rings of algebraic integers.
nt.divisibility.proof_idea: The Euclidean algorithm gives Bezout's identity; Euclid's lemma then proves uniqueness by induction.
nt.divisibility.prerequisites:
**From other subjects**

- [Sets, functions and relations](./notes/sl.sets.md) — Set theory and mathematical logic
nt.divisibility.references:
NT: unique factorization.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.crt.title: Chinese remainder theorem
nt.crt.define: Coprime congruence conditions combine into one unique residue class.
nt.crt.statement: For pairwise coprime positive integers $m_i$, $\mathbb Z/(\prod m_i)\cong\prod_i\mathbb Z/m_i$ as rings via the residue map.
nt.crt.hypotheses: Pairwise coprimality permits arbitrary independent residues.
nt.crt.caution: Without coprimality, residues must satisfy compatibility conditions.
nt.crt.proof_idea: Bezout coefficients construct idempotents selecting each coordinate.
nt.crt.references:
NT: Chinese remainder theorem.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.finite-fields.title: Finite fields
nt.finite-fields.define: Finite fields exist uniquely at prime-power sizes and have cyclic unit groups.
nt.finite-fields.statement: A finite field has $p^n$ elements. For each prime p and positive n there is exactly one up to isomorphism, the splitting field of $x^{p^n}-x$ over $\mathbb F_p$. Its multiplicative group is cyclic.
nt.finite-fields.hypotheses: Cardinality must be a prime power.
nt.finite-fields.caution: $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$ is not a field.
nt.finite-fields.proof_idea: Frobenius identifies the roots as a field; root bounds for polynomials prove multiplicative cyclicity.
nt.finite-fields.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Euclidean algorithm and unique factorization](./notes/nt.divisibility.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Groups and homomorphisms](./notes/gt.groups.md) — Group theory
nt.finite-fields.references:
FT: finite fields.

- **FT** — J. S. Milne. [Fields and Galois Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/FT.pdf). Version 5.10, 2022.

nt.reciprocity.title: Quadratic reciprocity
nt.reciprocity.define: Quadratic reciprocity relates square residues modulo two odd primes.
nt.reciprocity.statement: For distinct odd primes p,q, $(\frac pq)(\frac qp)=(-1)^{(p-1)(q-1)/4}$. Also $(\frac{-1}p)=(-1)^{(p-1)/2}$ and $(\frac2p)=(-1)^{(p^2-1)/8}$.
nt.reciprocity.hypotheses: The Legendre symbol is 1 for a nonzero square, -1 for a nonsquare, and 0 for a multiple of p.
nt.reciprocity.caution: A Jacobi symbol of one does not certify a square modulo a composite integer.
nt.reciprocity.proof_idea: Gauss's lemma turns the symbols into parity counts of lattice points.
nt.reciprocity.references:
NT2: quadratic reciprocity.

- **NT2** — Andrew V. Sutherland. [MIT 18.785: Number Theory I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-785-number-theory-i-fall-2021/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2021 lecture notes.

nt.number-fields.title: Number fields, norm and trace
nt.number-fields.define: Finite rational extensions carry field norms, traces and complex embeddings.
nt.number-fields.statement: A number field is a finite extension K of $\mathbb Q$. The determinant and trace of multiplication by a define $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(a)$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb Q}(a)$.
nt.number-fields.hypotheses: Characteristic zero ensures separability; the degree counts complex embeddings.
nt.number-fields.caution: Field norm is multiplicative, not a metric-space norm.
nt.number-fields.prerequisites:
**From other subjects**

- [Finite Galois correspondence](./notes/gt.galois.md) — Group theory
nt.number-fields.references:
NT: extensions, norms and traces.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.integers.title: Algebraic integers
nt.integers.define: Monic integer equations single out the integral arithmetic inside a number field.
nt.integers.statement: An element integral over $\mathbb Z$ satisfies a monic polynomial with integer coefficients. The integers of K form a ring $\mathcal O_K$, free of rank $[K:\mathbb Q]$ over $\mathbb Z$.
nt.integers.hypotheses: K is a number field; a rational algebraic integer is an integer.
nt.integers.caution: A field generator need not generate its entire ring of integers.
nt.integers.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Number fields, norm and trace](./notes/nt.number-fields.md)
nt.integers.references:
NT: rings of integers.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.discriminant.title: Trace pairing and discriminants
nt.discriminant.define: The trace pairing defines an arithmetic invariant of an integral basis.
nt.discriminant.statement: A basis $\omega_i$ has discriminant $\det(\operatorname{Tr}(\omega_i\omega_j))$. An integral basis defines the basis-independent field discriminant $d_K$.
nt.discriminant.hypotheses: A suborder's discriminant is the field discriminant times the square of its index.
nt.discriminant.caution: Polynomial and field discriminants can differ.
nt.discriminant.references:
NT: discriminants.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.ideals.title: Dedekind domains and ideal factorization
nt.ideals.define: The ring of integers of a number field is a Dedekind domain. Every nonzero proper ideal factors uniquely into nonzero prime ideals.
nt.ideals.statement: The ring of integers of a number field is a Dedekind domain. Every nonzero proper ideal factors uniquely into nonzero prime ideals.
nt.ideals.hypotheses: Dedekind here means Noetherian, integrally closed and dimension one.
nt.ideals.example: $\mathbb Z[\sqrt{-5}]$ has unique ideal factorization despite nonunique element factorization.
nt.ideals.caution: Unique ideal factorization does not imply every ideal is principal.
nt.ideals.proof_idea: Localize at nonzero primes to obtain discrete valuation rings and recover the ideal exponents.
nt.ideals.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Algebraic integers](./notes/nt.integers.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Noetherian rings and Hilbert basis theorem](./notes/ag.noetherian.md) — Algebraic geometry
nt.ideals.references:
NT: Dedekind domains.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.class-group.title: Ideal class group
nt.class-group.define: Ideal classes measure the obstruction to principal ideal factorization.
nt.class-group.statement: The group of nonzero fractional ideals modulo principal fractional ideals is $\operatorname{Cl}(K)$. It is trivial exactly when $\mathcal O_K$ is a PID, equivalently a UFD.
nt.class-group.hypotheses: Fractional ideals are invertible in a Dedekind domain.
nt.class-group.caution: Class number measures failure of principality, not the number of prime ideals.
nt.class-group.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Dedekind domains and ideal factorization](./notes/nt.ideals.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Normal subgroups and quotients](./notes/gt.quotients.md) — Group theory
nt.class-group.references:
NT: class groups.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.minkowski.title: Minkowski's theorem and finite class number
nt.minkowski.define: Large symmetric convex bodies contain lattice points, bounding ideal class representatives.
nt.minkowski.statement: A centrally symmetric convex measurable body in $\mathbb R^n$ of volume greater than $2^n\operatorname{covol}(\Lambda)$ contains a nonzero point of the full lattice $\Lambda$. This implies finiteness of $\operatorname{Cl}(K)$.
nt.minkowski.hypotheses: Strict inequality avoids boundary subtleties for nonclosed bodies.
nt.minkowski.example: Real and complex embeddings of ideals produce explicit bounds for ideal class representatives.
nt.minkowski.caution: Convexity and central symmetry are essential to this formulation.
nt.minkowski.proof_idea: Apply a lattice pigeonhole argument to half the body, then bound norms in inverse ideal classes.
nt.minkowski.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Ideal class group](./notes/nt.class-group.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Measure spaces](./notes/ra.measure.md) — Real analysis
nt.minkowski.references:
NT: geometry of numbers.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.units.title: Dirichlet's unit theorem
nt.units.define: The unit group has a finite torsion part and a rank determined by embeddings.
nt.units.statement: If K has $r_1$ real embeddings and $r_2$ conjugate pairs of complex embeddings, $\mathcal O_K^\times\cong\mu_K\times\mathbb Z^{r_1+r_2-1}$.
nt.units.hypotheses: The finite group of roots of unity is the torsion subgroup.
nt.units.caution: Computing fundamental units is a separate problem from determining their rank.
nt.units.proof_idea: The logarithmic embedding and geometry of numbers yield a full lattice in a hyperplane.
nt.units.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Algebraic integers](./notes/nt.integers.md)
- [Minkowski's theorem and finite class number](./notes/nt.minkowski.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Finitely generated abelian groups](./notes/gt.abelian-structure.md) — Group theory
nt.units.references:
NT: units.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.padic.title: p-adic numbers and Hensel lifting
nt.padic.define: Prime-adic completion supports lifting simple polynomial roots to exact roots.
nt.padic.statement: Complete $\mathbb Q$ for $|x|_p=p^{-v_p(x)}$ to obtain $\mathbb Q_p$. If $f\in\mathbb Z_p[x]$, $f(a)\equiv0\pmod p$ and $f'(a)\not\equiv0\pmod p$, f has a unique root congruent to a modulo p in $\mathbb Z_p$.
nt.padic.hypotheses: This is the simple-root form of Hensel's lemma.
nt.padic.example: $x^2-2$ has a root in $\mathbb Z_7$ lifting 3 modulo 7.
nt.padic.caution: A multiple root modulo p need not lift by this criterion.
nt.padic.proof_idea: Newton iteration improves the p-adic error and converges by completeness.
nt.padic.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Euclidean algorithm and unique factorization](./notes/nt.divisibility.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Metric limits and completeness](./notes/ra.metric.md) — Real analysis
nt.padic.references:
NT: completions and Hensel lemma.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.ramification.title: Splitting and ramification
nt.ramification.define: Prime ideals describe splitting, residue degrees and ramification of rational primes.
nt.ramification.statement: In $\mathcal O_K$, $p\mathcal O_K=\prod_i\mathfrak p_i^{e_i}$ with residue degrees $f_i$ and $\sum_i e_if_i=[K:\mathbb Q]$. A rational prime ramifies exactly when it divides $d_K$.
nt.ramification.hypotheses: Use the full ring of integers of a number field.
nt.ramification.caution: Factoring a defining polynomial can mislead at primes dividing the index of the chosen order.
nt.ramification.proof_idea: Compare residue-field dimensions and detect ramification through the trace pairing.
nt.ramification.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Dedekind domains and ideal factorization](./notes/nt.ideals.md)
- [Trace pairing and discriminants](./notes/nt.discriminant.md)
- [Finite fields](./notes/nt.finite-fields.md)
nt.ramification.references:
NT: prime decomposition.

- **NT** — J. S. Milne. [Algebraic Number Theory](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf). Version 3.08, 2020.

nt.zeta.title: Riemann zeta function
nt.zeta.define: The zeta function connects integer summation with an Euler product over primes.
nt.zeta.statement: For $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-s}=\prod_p(1-p^{-s})^{-1}$. It extends meromorphically to the plane with only a simple pole at 1, of residue one.
nt.zeta.hypotheses: Absolute convergence of the series and product holds in the stated half-plane.
nt.zeta.example: The logarithmic derivative encodes prime powers.
nt.zeta.caution: Continuation does not justify using a divergent Euler product term by term.
nt.zeta.proof_idea: Unique factorization gives the product; integral representations provide continuation.
nt.zeta.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Euclidean algorithm and unique factorization](./notes/nt.divisibility.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Analytic continuation and monodromy](./notes/ca.continuation.md) — Complex analysis
nt.zeta.references:
NT2: zeta function.

- **NT2** — Andrew V. Sutherland. [MIT 18.785: Number Theory I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-785-number-theory-i-fall-2021/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2021 lecture notes.

nt.dirichlet-characters.title: Dirichlet characters and L-functions
nt.dirichlet-characters.define: Multiplicative characters separate residue classes through their L-functions.
nt.dirichlet-characters.statement: A character modulo q is a character of $(\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z)^\times$, extended by zero on nonunits. For $\operatorname{Re}s>1$, $L(s,\chi)=\sum_{n\ge1}\chi(n)n^{-s}$.
nt.dirichlet-characters.hypotheses: Distinguish primitive characters from characters induced from smaller moduli.
nt.dirichlet-characters.example: Character orthogonality isolates reduced residue classes.
nt.dirichlet-characters.caution: The principal character has Euler factors removed at primes dividing q.
nt.dirichlet-characters.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Riemann zeta function](./notes/nt.zeta.md)
- [Chinese remainder theorem](./notes/nt.crt.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Characters and orthogonality](./notes/gt.characters.md) — Group theory
nt.dirichlet-characters.references:
NT2: Dirichlet characters.

- **NT2** — Andrew V. Sutherland. [MIT 18.785: Number Theory I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-785-number-theory-i-fall-2021/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2021 lecture notes.

nt.dirichlet.title: Dirichlet's theorem on primes
nt.dirichlet.define: Every residue class coprime to its modulus contains infinitely many primes.
nt.dirichlet.statement: If $\gcd(a,q)=1$ and $q\ge1$, infinitely many primes satisfy $p\equiv a\pmod q$.
nt.dirichlet.hypotheses: The residue class is coprime to the modulus.
nt.dirichlet.example: There are infinitely many primes congruent to 3 modulo 4.
nt.dirichlet.caution: Infinitude alone supplies no asymptotic count.
nt.dirichlet.proof_idea: Use character orthogonality and nonvanishing of nonprincipal L-functions at one.
nt.dirichlet.references:
NT2: primes in progressions.

- **NT2** — Andrew V. Sutherland. [MIT 18.785: Number Theory I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-785-number-theory-i-fall-2021/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2021 lecture notes.

nt.pnt.title: Prime number theorem
nt.pnt.define: The counting function of primes has a logarithmic asymptotic density.
nt.pnt.statement: If $\pi(x)$ counts primes at most x, then $\pi(x)\sim x/\log x$ as $x\to\infty$.
nt.pnt.hypotheses: The logarithm is natural; no error term is claimed here.
nt.pnt.example: The average spacing of primes near x has scale log x.
nt.pnt.caution: The theorem does not bound each prime gap by a fixed multiple of log x.
nt.pnt.proof_idea: An analytic proof combines nonvanishing of zeta on Re s = 1 with a Tauberian theorem.
nt.pnt.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Riemann zeta function](./notes/nt.zeta.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Residue theorem](./notes/ca.residues.md) — Complex analysis
nt.pnt.references:
NT2: prime number theorem.

- **NT2** — Andrew V. Sutherland. [MIT 18.785: Number Theory I](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-785-number-theory-i-fall-2021/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2021 lecture notes.

nt.elliptic.title: Elliptic curves and rational points
nt.elliptic.define: A pointed smooth projective genus-one curve carries an arithmetic group law.
nt.elliptic.statement: An elliptic curve over K is a smooth projective geometrically integral genus-one curve with a chosen K-rational point. In characteristic different from 2 and 3 it has a model $y^2=x^3+Ax+B$, $4A^3+27B^2\ne0$.
nt.elliptic.hypotheses: The projective point at infinity is the identity in this model.
nt.elliptic.example: Chords and tangents describe the group law.
nt.elliptic.caution: A singular cubic is not an elliptic curve.
nt.elliptic.prerequisites:
**From other subjects**

- [Smooth projective curves and genus](./notes/ag.curves.md) — Algebraic geometry
- [Groups and homomorphisms](./notes/gt.groups.md) — Group theory
nt.elliptic.references:
EC: elliptic curves.

- **EC** — J. S. Milne. [Elliptic Curves](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/EC2.pdf). Second edition, World Scientific, 2020; author-hosted text.

nt.mordell-weil.title: Mordell–Weil theorem
nt.mordell-weil.define: Rational points on an elliptic curve over a number field are finitely generated.
nt.mordell-weil.statement: For an elliptic curve E over a number field K, $E(K)$ is a finitely generated abelian group.
nt.mordell-weil.hypotheses: E is nonsingular and K is a number field.
nt.mordell-weil.caution: Finite generation does not mean finitely many rational points or an easy rank computation.
nt.mordell-weil.proof_idea: Finite descent classes and height reduction establish finite generation.
nt.mordell-weil.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Elliptic curves and rational points](./notes/nt.elliptic.md)
- [Number fields, norm and trace](./notes/nt.number-fields.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Finitely generated abelian groups](./notes/gt.abelian-structure.md) — Group theory
nt.mordell-weil.references:
EC: Mordell-Weil theorem.

- **EC** — J. S. Milne. [Elliptic Curves](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/EC2.pdf). Second edition, World Scientific, 2020; author-hosted text.

nt.local-global.title: Local–global principles and limits
nt.local-global.define: A nondegenerate quadratic form over a number field has a nonzero zero if and only if it has one over every completion.
nt.local-global.statement: A nondegenerate quadratic form over a number field has a nonzero zero if and only if it has one over every completion.
nt.local-global.hypotheses: The Hasse–Minkowski theorem includes every finite and Archimedean place.
nt.local-global.example: Projective conics can be tested over completions.
nt.local-global.caution: Genus-one torsors can have points over every completion but no rational point.
nt.local-global.proof_idea: Local classification of quadratic forms combines with global reciprocity; the global-to-local direction is immediate.
nt.local-global.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [p-adic numbers and Hensel lifting](./notes/nt.padic.md)
- [Number fields, norm and trace](./notes/nt.number-fields.md)
nt.local-global.references:
NT3: Hasse-Minkowski theorem; EC: genus-one curves.

- **NT3** — Keith Conrad. [The Local–Global Principle](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/localglobal.pdf). Author's expository notes; quadratic forms and failures of local-global principles.
- **EC** — J. S. Milne. [Elliptic Curves](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/EC2.pdf). Second edition, World Scientific, 2020; author-hosted text.
